items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: Like Art Blakey with the Jazz Messengers. He was one of the greater leaders of all time.

ctx.x: You know not just in the classroom.

You know what I find is that a lot of band leaders are not drummers and they do not know how to tell their drummers what to do. So I just had the pleasure of writing an article in DownBeat magazine on how to lead a band from the drum chair. Now you could have the greatest band, the greatest arrangements, the greatest soloists, but if you have a mediocre drummer then you have a mediocre band. Now I’m here to tell you that drummers should unite and start to put together certain musical aggregations that they can…

away from the far out bebop and just get in to the hard-driving, high energy swing that makes you laugh because it’s so happy. You know people have to not take themselves so seriously sometimes on a bandstand. And I think it would be to the benefit of the audience too, overall.
